title: Investigation of epigenetic targets in myeloid malignancies
summary: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a life-threatening form of blood cancer in which malignant cells proliferate in the bone marrow and displace normal blood formation. Research over recent decades has significantly advanced our understanding of AML. However, many open questions remain, which we are also trying to answer through research projects at our clinic. Our overarching goal is to develop new diagnostic and therapeutic strategies through clinical and experimental research. Research in recent years has shown that epigenetic changes contribute to leukemia cells evading therapy. We want to find out which epigenetic changes play a role in AML and how these can be utilized for new therapeutic approaches. We aim to achieve this by analyzing the blood of patients with AML in greater detail.
